title: NMR Chemical Shift Peak Assignment Tool
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive NMR (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance) Chemical Shift Peak Assignment Tool. The scene combines a 3D molecular viewer with a 2D NMR spectrum chart rendered as a 3D plane.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark background (0x1a1a2e). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.6) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.9) from (5, 8, 5).
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## 3D Molecular Model (Ethanol: CH3-CH2-OH)
- Build a 3D ball-and-stick model of ethanol on the LEFT side of the scene (centered at x=-3).
- Atoms as spheres: Carbon (gray 0x555555, radius 0.35), Hydrogen (white 0xeeeeee, radius 0.2), Oxygen (red 0xcc0000, radius 0.32).
- Bonds as thin cylinders (radius 0.06, white) connecting atoms.
- Atom positions (approximate):
  - C1 (methyl carbon): (-3, 0, 0)
  - C2 (methylene carbon): (-1.5, 0, 0)
  - O1 (hydroxyl oxygen): (-0.3, 0.5, 0)
  - H atoms on C1: (-3.6, 0.7, 0.5), (-3.6, -0.5, 0.6), (-3.6, 0, -0.7)
  - H atoms on C2: (-1.5, 0.8, 0.7), (-1.5, -0.8, 0.7)
  - H on O1: (0.3, 1.1, 0)
- Each atom mesh should have userData = { element: 'C'|'H'|'O', label: 'C1'|'C2'|'O1'|'H1a'|'H1b'|'H1c'|'H2a'|'H2b'|'OH', group: 'methyl'|'methylene'|'hydroxyl' }.
- When an atom is hovered, apply emissive glow (emissive color 0xffff00, emissive intensity 0.4). Remove glow on mouse leave.

## NMR Spectrum Display (RIGHT side)
- Create a flat PlaneGeometry (5, 3) at position (3.5, 0, 0) rotated to face the camera.
- On this plane, render an NMR spectrum using CanvasTexture (a 2D canvas of 800x400 pixels).
- The spectrum X-axis represents chemical shift in ppm from 0 to 5 (right to left, as is convention in NMR).
- Draw three peaks as Gaussian curves on the canvas:
  - Peak A: center=1.2 ppm, height=0.9 (normalized), width_sigma=0.08 — corresponds to CH3 (methyl) protons (triplet pattern simplified as single peak)
  - Peak B: center=3.7 ppm, height=0.7, width_sigma=0.08 — corresponds to CH2 (methylene) protons
  - Peak C: center=2.6 ppm, height=0.3, width_sigma=0.06 — corresponds to OH proton
- Draw axis labels: 'Chemical Shift (ppm)' on X-axis, 'Intensity' on Y-axis. Mark ppm values 0,1,2,3,4,5.
- Peaks should be drawn in a spectrum color (green line on dark background).

## Peak Assignment Interaction
- Implement a mode system: 'view' mode (default) and 'assign' mode.
- A DOM button 'Toggle Assign Mode' switches between modes. In assign mode, the button should show 'Assign Mode: ON' with a yellow background.
- In assign mode:
  1. User clicks on an atom in the 3D model — it becomes 'selected' (highlighted with outline or bright emissive 0x00ff00). Store selectedAtom.
  2. User then clicks on the spectrum plane — use raycasting to determine the ppm value of the click. Find the nearest peak (within 0.5 ppm tolerance). If a peak is found, create an assignment linking the atom group to that peak.
  3. When an assignment is made, draw a colored line (as a Line geometry) from the atom position to the corresponding peak position on the spectrum plane. Use color coding: methyl=0x00aaff, methylene=0xff8800, hydroxyl=0xff00ff.
  4. The spectrum canvas should update to show the assignment label above the peak (e.g., 'CH3', 'CH2', 'OH').
- A 'Clear Assignments' button removes all assignment lines and labels.
- A 'Validate' button checks if all three peaks are correctly assigned and shows result.

## Peak Integration Display
- Below the spectrum, show a DOM panel (#integration-panel) displaying integration ratios.
- When peaks are assigned, show: 'CH3: 3H', 'CH2: 2H', 'OH: 1H' with a ratio display '3:2:1'.
- Integration values update as assignments are made.

## Scoring System
- Track correct assignments: methyl↔Peak A (1.2 ppm), methylene↔Peak B (3.7 ppm), hydroxyl↔Peak C (2.6 ppm).
- When Validate is clicked, compute score: each correct assignment = 1 point (max 3). Display score in a DOM element (#score-display).

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- mode: 'view' | 'assign' (current interaction mode)
- selectedAtom: null | { label: string, group: string, element: string } (currently selected atom)
- peaks: [ { id: 'A', center_ppm: 1.2, height: 0.9, sigma: 0.08, assignedGroup: null|string }, { id: 'B', center_ppm: 3.7, height: 0.7, sigma: 0.08, assignedGroup: null|string }, { id: 'C', center_ppm: 2.6, height: 0.3, sigma: 0.06, assignedGroup: null|string } ]
- assignments: [] (array of { atomGroup: string, peakId: string, ppm: number })
- assignmentLines: number (count of visible assignment lines in scene)
- score: null | number (null before validation, 0-3 after)
- validated: boolean
- hoveredAtom: null | string (label of currently hovered atom)
- atomCount: number (total atoms in molecule, should be 9)
- bondCount: number (total bonds, should be 8)
- integrationRatios: { methyl: number, methylene: number, hydroxyl: number } (hydrogen counts: 3, 2, 1)
- spectrumRendered: boolean (true after canvas texture is drawn)
- peakPositions: [ { id: string, ppm: number } ] (the three peak center positions)

Ensure __3D_STATE__ is updated in real-time as interactions occur.
physics_constraints: NMR chemical shifts must follow standard ethanol 1H-NMR values: methyl ~1.2 ppm, methylene ~3.7 ppm, hydroxyl ~2.6 ppm. Integration ratios must be 3:2:1 for CH3:CH2:OH. Peak positions on the spectrum must map linearly to the 0-5 ppm axis. Gaussian peak shapes must have correct sigma values. Assignment validation must enforce exact group-to-peak mapping.
